The pull_naturality field of DivRepAffinePullback compares the forward map at A with the
forward map at B along phi : A -> B. The forward map is built from an atlas factorization
over a spanning family f : Fin m -> A, so naturality needs the PUSHED family phi . f and the
induced comparison of carriers. This isolates that localization bookkeeping.

  awayPush                 -- Localization.Away a ->alg[k] Localization.Away (phi a), i.e.
                              mathlib's Localization.awayMap upgraded over the base field
                              (both structure maps factor through phi)
  awayPush_algebraMap      -- its characterizing property on the image of A
  awayPush_comp_toAlgHom   -- THE NATURALITY SQUARE of the carriers: restrict-then-push =
                              phi-then-restrict.  This is the identity that turns
                              pull_naturality into a comparison over the pushed cover.
  span_range_map_eq_top    -- the pushed family still spans, so an away cover pushes
                              forward to an away cover

Nothing here mentions divisors; keeping it separate lets the naturality proof itself read as
a comparison of glued values rather than as localization plumbing.

DivisorFamilyAffZar import is in the worktree copy and is deliberately not swept, protocol
section 4).

Archon-Commit: agent
Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>")

1	---
2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a `"$HORIZON_BIN" task comment <task_id> --body …`
148	at each significant step. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
281	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
282	  as **memory**.
283	
284	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
285	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
286	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
287	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
288	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
289	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
290	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
291	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
292	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
293	
294	## Resuming after an interruption
295	
296	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
297	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
298	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
299	
300	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
301	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
302	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
303	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
304	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
305	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
306	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
307	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
308	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
309	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
310	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
311	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
312	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
313	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
314	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
315	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
316	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
317	
318	## Final report (your last message)
319	
320	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
321	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
322	Recommended sections: `## Summary`, `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
323	`## Why I stopped`, `## Next` (keep at least `## Progress` and
324	`## Why I stopped`). In `## Progress`, one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
325	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
326	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
327	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
328	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
329	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
330	not by itself a reason to stop.
331	
332	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
333	
334	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
335	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
336	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
337	`subagents` skill):
338	
339	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
340	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
341	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
342	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
343	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
344	
345	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.
346

---
name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

=== ENV ===
ARCHON_HORIZON_AGENT_ROLE=horizon
ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS=Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT=/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND=0
ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS=8
ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN=0071
ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION=0002-horizon-ajcr-divrep
ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR=/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.archon-horizon/runs/0071/sessions/0002-horizon-ajcr-divrep
ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL=/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md
ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK=ajcr-divrep
ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE=divRep and the datum tail: Div^g-lite representability through to the Pic^0 datum
HORIZON_BIN=/home/axel/.archon-env/bin/horizon
HORIZON_GIT=/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.archon-horizon/bin/hgit
HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR=/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE=/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
PATH=/home/axel/.archon-env/bin:/home/axel/.archon-env/bin:/home/axel/.local/bin:/home/axel/.npm-global/bin:/home/axel/.vscode-server/data/User/globalStorage/github.copilot-chat/debugCommand:/home/axel/.vscode-server/data/User/globalStorage/github.copilot-chat/copilotCli:/home/axel/.vscode-server/cli/servers/Stable-8b640eef5a6c6089c029249d48efa5c99adf7d51/server/bin/remote-cli:/home/axel/.local/bin:/home/axel/.elan/bin:/home/axel/.npm-global/bin:/home/axel/.local/bin:/home/axel/.local/bin:/home/axel/.npm-global/bin:/home/axel/.local/bin:/home/axel/.elan/bin:/home/axel/.npm-global/bin:/home/axel/.local/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/games:/usr/local/games:/snap/bin

73	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
74	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm)
75	
76	local notation "ChartRing" => fun i j =>
77	  DivCarveChartRing k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
78	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
79	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j
80	
81	local notation "ChartMap" => fun i j =>
82	  divCarveChartToDivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
83	    (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
84	    (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm) i j
85	
86	/-! ## F5: pullback from one supplied universal chart family -/
87	
88	/-- Pull a supplied Zariski-locally certified **class** on one carve chart to a test
89	algebra.  This is the choice-free per-chart operation from which F5's affine forward map
90	is glued.
91	
92	The supplied datum is a `DivFamZar` class, not a globally certified family: the forward
93	map only ever transports a class along `DivFamZar.mapAlgHom`, so a global degree-`g`
94	certificate over the chart ring is never consumed.  A caller that does hold a
95	`CertifiedDivisorFamily G` on a chart passes `(DivFam.mk G).toZar`, so no expressive
96	power is lost, while the Zariski-local production rules (`IsLocallyCertified`) become
97	usable here. -/
98	noncomputable def divRepPullAt
99	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
100	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
101	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
102	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
103	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) : DivFamZar C S pi g :=
104	  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom omega (U i j)
105	
106	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
107	@[simp]
108	theorem divRepPullAt_id
109	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
110	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
111	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J) :
112	    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (AlgHom.id k (ChartRing i j))
113	      = U i j :=
114	  DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_id _
115	
116	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
117	/-- Pulling a chart class through two algebra maps is the same as pulling it through
118	their composite.  This is the algebraic part of F5 naturality. -/
119	theorem divRepPullAt_comp
120	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
121	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
122	    {S T : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] [CommRing T] [Algebra k T]
123	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
124	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (phi : S →ₐ[k] T) :
125	    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega)
126	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j (phi.comp omega) :=
127	  (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_comp omega phi (U i j)).symm
128	
129	namespace DivRepChartFamily
130	
131	/-- The precise F5 overlap obligation for a supplied family of classes on every carve
132	chart: two chart points inducing the same morphism to `DivScheme` have equal pulled
133	locally certified divisor classes.  The future universal-family construction proves this
134	from its epsilon identity and the total mono theorem. -/
135	def IsCompatible
136	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
137	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g) : Prop :=
138	  ∀ {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
139	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
140	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
141	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S),
142	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j
143	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' →
144	      divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
145	        = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega'
146	
147	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
148	/-- Compatibility may be applied when both chart presentations are identified with a
149	common morphism.  This is the form used on overlaps of an atlas factorization. -/
150	theorem pullAt_eq_of_eq_common
151	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
152	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
153	    (hU : IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
154	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
155	    (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J)
156	    (i' : (glueData k g r1).J) (j' : (glueData k g r2).J)
157	    (omega : ChartRing i j →ₐ[k] S) (omega' : ChartRing i' j' →ₐ[k] S)
158	    (q : Spec (CommRingCat.of S) ⟶
159	      DivScheme k (windowS_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi)
160	        (windowM_choice pi hpi g • fiberWeilDivisor pi) g r1 r2 b1
161	        (b2.map (windowShiftEquiv hpi g).symm))
162	    (homega : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i j = q)
163	    (homega' : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom omega'.toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap i' j' = q) :
164	    divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i j omega
165	      = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U i' j' omega' :=
166	  hU i j i' j' omega omega' (homega.trans homega'.symm)
167	
168	end DivRepChartFamily
169	
170	/-! ## F6: package a completed affine pullback as an equivalence -/
171	
172	/-- The exact output expected from F5 before the affine equivalence is packaged.
173	`isDivRepClassify_pull` is the hom-side law in the refinement-stable clause spelling;
174	classifier uniqueness turns it into the second inverse law automatically. -/
175	structure DivRepAffinePullback where
176	  pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S],
177	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) → DivFamZar C S pi g
178	  pull_classify : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
179	    (F : DivFamZar C S pi g),
180	    pull S (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F) = F
181	  isDivRepClassify_pull : ∀ (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
182	    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver),
183	    IsDivRepClassify hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 (pull S v) v.left
184	  pull_naturality : ∀ {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
185	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver),
186	    pull B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v) = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi (pull A v)
187	
188	namespace DivRepAffinePullback
189	
190	/-- The affine representability equivalence assembled from an F5 pullback package.
191	The inverse is the landed backward classifier; its hom-side inverse law follows from
192	`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`. -/
193	noncomputable def equiv
194	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
195	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] :
196	    (overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) ≃ DivFamZar C S pi g where
197	  toFun := D.pull S
198	  invFun := divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S
199	  left_inv v :=
200	    (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2
201	      (D.pull S v) v (D.isDivRepClassify_pull S v)).symm
202	  right_inv := D.pull_classify S
203	
204	@[simp]
205	theorem equiv_apply
206	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
207	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver) :
208	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
209	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S v = D.pull S v :=
210	  rfl
211	
212	@[simp]
213	theorem equiv_symm_apply
214	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
215	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (F : DivFamZar C S pi g) :
216	    (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
217	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D S).symm F
218	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 S F :=
219	  rfl
220	
221	/-- Naturality of the assembled affine equivalence, in the frozen DDR-9 spelling. -/
222	theorem equiv_naturality
223	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
224	    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
225	    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (phi : A →ₐ[k] B)
226	    (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver) :
227	    equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
228	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D B (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ v)
229	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi
230	          (equiv (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
231	            (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D A v) :=
232	  D.pull_naturality phi v
233	
234	end DivRepAffinePullback

9	/-!
10	# The away-span glue of locally certified classes at CANONICAL carriers
11	
12	The S5b keystone `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat`
13	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyZarGlue.lean`) glues over an away cover whose carriers `S i` and
14	overlap carriers `T i j` are supplied *as instance data* — eight
15	`Algebra`/`IsScalarTower` fields per index pair.  Every consumer that starts from a
16	bare spanning family `f : Fin m → S`, which is what the atlas factorization
17	`divScheme_exists_chartFactor` (`Picard/DivSchemeAtlasFactor.lean`) hands back, must
18	build that pack itself before it can glue anything.
19	
20	This file builds the pack once, at the **canonical** carriers
21	`Localization.Away (f p)` and `Localization.Away (f p * f q)`, and restates the two
22	keystones so that a consumer holding only `f` and `Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤` can
23	use them:
24	
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.awayMulOfDvd` — the comparison `k`-algebra map
26	  `Localization.Away a →ₐ[k] Localization.Away f` attached to a factorization
27	  `a * b = f`, from `IsLocalization.Away.lift` at the unit
28	  `algebraMap S (Localization.Away f) a`; `awayMulLeft`/`awayMulRight` are its two
29	  instances at the overlap of a pair.
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_awaySpan` — **existence**: locally
31	  certified classes `F p` over `Localization.Away (f p)`, agreeing after base change
32	  along `awayMulLeft`/`awayMulRight` into each `Localization.Away (f p * f q)`, glue to
33	  a class over `S` restricting to every `F p`.
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.eq_of_awaySpan_eq` — **separation** in the same
35	  spelling.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.existsUnique_glue_of_awaySpan` — the two combined, in
37	  the `∃!` form the DDR-9 forward map's choice bookkeeping consumes (`w4-ddr9`
38	  worksheet §3.4): it is what makes a glued value independent of every choice made in
39	  producing the cover.
40	
41	Two design points, both deliberate.  The overlap carrier is the canonical
42	`Localization.Away (f p * f q)` rather than a tensor product, which is what makes the
43	instance pack derivable at all: it receives both away carriers by
44	`IsLocalization.Away.lift` against the divisibility witnesses `f p ∣ f p * f q` and
45	`f q ∣ f p * f q`, and the tower coherences then reduce to
46	`IsLocalization.Away.lift_comp` plus the landed `isScalarTower_left_of_isScalarTower`.
47	And the *statements* are spelled with `DivFamZar.mapAlgHom` along an explicit `AlgHom`
48	rather than with the instance-parameterized `DivFamZar.mapAlg`: a caller then needs no
49	algebra instances in scope at all, and the face-change bridge
50	`DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg` moves each hypothesis onto the instance face inside the
51	proof, where the pack is available.
52	-/
53	
54	set_option autoImplicit false
55	/- Statements mix `Γ(relCurve C R, ·)` with opens produced on the product spelling
56	`(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`; see `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.RelativeSectionsLinear`. -/
57	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
58	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161), so the pinned synthesis
59	depth must be set in-file for the faithful per-file check. -/
60	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
61	
62	universe u
63	
64	open CategoryTheory
65	
66	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
67	
68	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
69	
70	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
71	variable {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
72	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}
73	
74	namespace DivFamZar
75	
76	/-! ## The comparison map into a canonical away localization at a multiple -/
77	
78	/-- **The comparison map of a factorization**: for `a * b = f`, the canonical away
79	localization at `f` receives the one at `a`, because `algebraMap S (Localization.Away f) a`
80	is a unit (`IsLocalization.Away.isUnit_of_dvd`) so `IsLocalization.Away.lift` applies.
81	It is a map of `k`-algebras because both structure maps factor through `S`. -/
82	noncomputable def awayMulOfDvd (f a b : S) (h : a * b = f) :
83	    Localization.Away a →ₐ[k] Localization.Away f :=
84	  { IsLocalization.Away.lift a (S := Localization.Away a)
85	      (g := algebraMap S (Localization.Away f))
86	      (IsLocalization.Away.isUnit_of_dvd (x := f) ⟨b, h.symm⟩) with
87	    commutes' := fun x => by
88	      rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k S (Localization.Away a)]
89	      change IsLocalization.Away.lift a _ (algebraMap S (Localization.Away a) _) = _
90	      rw [IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq]
91	      exact (IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k S (Localization.Away f) x).symm }
92	
93	/-- **The comparison map is the localization lift**: it agrees with
94	`algebraMap S (Localization.Away f)` on `S`, which characterizes it. -/
95	@[simp]
96	theorem awayMulOfDvd_algebraMap (f a b : S) (h : a * b = f) (x : S) :
97	    awayMulOfDvd (k := k) f a b h (algebraMap S (Localization.Away a) x)
98	      = algebraMap S (Localization.Away f) x :=
99	  IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq a
100	    (IsLocalization.Away.isUnit_of_dvd (S := Localization.Away f) (x := f) ⟨b, h.symm⟩) x
101	
102	set_option maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
103	-- The composite is checked against the `IsScalarTower` structure map of the localization,
104	-- which unfolds the section-ring algebra tower on both sides; the defeq check is well
105	-- past the default budget (measured: over 800000 heartbeats).
106	/-- **The comparison map is a map over the base ring**: composing the structure map
107	`S → Localization.Away a` with the comparison into `Localization.Away f` gives the
108	structure map `S → Localization.Away f`.  This is the form consumed when a class pulled
109	back from `S` is compared across two different away localizations. -/
110	theorem awayMulOfDvd_toAlgHom (f a b : S) (h : a * b = f) (x : S) :
111	    awayMulOfDvd (k := k) f a b h (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away a) x)
112	      = IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away f) x :=
113	  IsLocalization.Away.lift_eq a
114	    (IsLocalization.Away.isUnit_of_dvd (S := Localization.Away f) (x := f) ⟨b, h.symm⟩) x
115	
116	section Pack
117	
118	variable {m : ℕ} (f : Fin m → S)
119	
120	/-- The left comparison into the canonical overlap carrier of the pair `(p, q)`. -/
121	noncomputable abbrev awayMulLeft (p q : Fin m) :
122	    Localization.Away (f p) →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f p * f q) :=
123	  awayMulOfDvd (f p * f q) (f p) (f q) rfl
124	
125	/-- The right comparison into the canonical overlap carrier of the pair `(p, q)`. -/
126	noncomputable abbrev awayMulRight (p q : Fin m) :
127	    Localization.Away (f q) →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f p * f q) :=
128	  awayMulOfDvd (f p * f q) (f q) (f p) (mul_comm _ _)
129	
130	end Pack
131	
132	/-! ## Existence -/
133	
134	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
135	-- Eight `Algebra`/`IsScalarTower` fields are discharged in the body at the canonical
136	-- carriers, and each unifies the section-ring algebra towers of two away localizations
137	-- at once; the defeq checks exceed the default budget (as in
138	-- `divFamZar.exists_isGlueValue` and `DivRepClassifyZar.exists_isDivRepClassify`).
139	/-- **The away-span glue at canonical carriers**: locally certified divisor classes over
140	the canonical away localizations of a finite spanning family `f`, agreeing after base
141	change along the two comparison maps into each canonical overlap localization
142	`Localization.Away (f p * f q)`, glue to a class over `S` restricting to each of them.
143	
144	This is the S5b keystone `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat` with its instance pack
145	discharged at the canonical carriers: the overlap carrier receives both away carriers by
146	the comparison maps, the `S`-towers are `awayMulOfDvd_algebraMap`, and the `k`-towers are
147	the `AlgHom` commutation of the same maps.  Hypothesis and conclusion are stated on the
148	explicit `mapAlgHom` face and moved onto the instance face by the face-change bridge
149	`mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg`, so no caller needs the pack. -/
150	theorem exists_glue_of_awaySpan {m : ℕ} (f : Fin m → S)
151	    (hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
152	    (F : ∀ p : Fin m, DivFamZar C (Localization.Away (f p)) π n)
153	    (hcompat : ∀ p q : Fin m,
154	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (awayMulLeft (k := k) f p q) (F p)
155	        = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (awayMulRight (k := k) f p q) (F q)) :
156	    ∃ F₀ : DivFamZar C S π n, ∀ p : Fin m,
157	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away (f p))) F₀ = F p := by
158	  classical
159	  -- the overlap carrier receives both away carriers, by the two comparison maps
160	  letI algL : ∀ p q : Fin m, Algebra (Localization.Away (f p))
161	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) := fun p q =>
162	    (awayMulLeft (k := k) f p q).toRingHom.toAlgebra
163	  letI algR : ∀ p q : Fin m, Algebra (Localization.Away (f q))
164	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) := fun p q =>
165	    (awayMulRight (k := k) f p q).toRingHom.toAlgebra
166	  -- the `S`-towers: each comparison map is the localization lift
167	  haveI towSL : ∀ p q : Fin m, IsScalarTower S (Localization.Away (f p))
168	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) := fun p q =>
169	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (RingHom.ext fun x => by
170	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
171	      exact (awayMulOfDvd_algebraMap (k := k) (f p * f q) (f p) (f q) rfl x).symm)
172	  haveI towSR : ∀ p q : Fin m, IsScalarTower S (Localization.Away (f q))
173	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) := fun p q =>
174	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (RingHom.ext fun x => by
175	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
176	      exact (awayMulOfDvd_algebraMap (k := k) (f p * f q) (f q) (f p)
177	        (mul_comm _ _) x).symm)
178	  -- the `k`-towers: the comparison maps are maps of `k`-algebras
179	  haveI towkL : ∀ p q : Fin m, IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away (f p))
180	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) := fun p q =>
181	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (RingHom.ext fun x => by
182	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
183	      exact ((awayMulLeft (k := k) f p q).commutes x).symm)
184	  haveI towkR : ∀ p q : Fin m, IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away (f q))
185	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) := fun p q =>
186	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (RingHom.ext fun x => by
187	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
188	      exact ((awayMulRight (k := k) f p q).commutes x).symm)
189	  -- the keystone, with the hypothesis transported onto the instance face.  The
190	  -- compatibility proof is deferred with `?_` so that the carrier families are fixed
191	  -- before it elaborates (otherwise `mapAlg`'s instance arguments stay metavariables).
192	  have hkey : ∀ l l' : ULift.{u} (Fin m),
193	      DivFamZar.mapAlg (C := C) (π := π)
194	          (Localization.Away (f l.down * f l'.down)) n (F l.down)
195	        = DivFamZar.mapAlg (C := C) (π := π)
196	          (Localization.Away (f l.down * f l'.down)) n (F l'.down) := by
197	    intro l l'
198	    rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg (awayMulLeft (k := k) f l.down l'.down)
199	        (fun _ => rfl),
200	      ← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg (awayMulRight (k := k) f l.down l'.down)
201	        (fun _ => rfl)]
202	    exact hcompat l.down l'.down
203	  -- the keystone indexes over `Type u`, so the cover is reindexed by `ULift (Fin m)`
204	  obtain ⟨F₀, hF₀⟩ := DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_away_compat
205	    (fun l : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => f l.down)
206	    (fun l : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => Localization.Away (f l.down))
207	    (fun l l' : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => Localization.Away (f l.down * f l'.down))
208	    (by
209	      rw [show (Set.range fun l : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => f l.down) = Set.range f from
210	        ULift.down_surjective.range_comp f]
211	      exact hspan)
212	    (fun l => F l.down) hkey
213	  refine ⟨F₀, fun p => ?_⟩
214	  have hF₀p := hF₀ (ULift.up p)
215	  rw [DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away (f p)))
216	    (fun _ => rfl)]
217	  exact hF₀p
218	
219	/-! ## Separation -/
220	
221	/-- **Separation in the canonical-carrier spelling**: two locally certified classes over
222	`S` agreeing after base change to every `Localization.Away (f p)` of a finite spanning
223	family agree — `DivFamZar.eq_of_away_eq` at the canonical carriers, whose instance pack
224	is the ambient one, with the hypothesis read on the explicit `mapAlgHom` face. -/
225	theorem eq_of_awaySpan_eq {ι : Type} [Finite ι] (f : ι → S)
226	    (hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
227	    {F G : DivFamZar C S π n}
228	    (h : ∀ p : ι,
229	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away (f p))) F
230	        = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away (f p))) G) :
231	    F = G := by
232	  -- the keystone indexes over `Type u`, so the cover is reindexed by `ULift ι`
233	  refine DivFamZar.eq_of_away_eq (fun l : ULift.{u} ι => f l.down)
234	    (fun l : ULift.{u} ι => Localization.Away (f l.down))
235	    (by
236	      rw [show (Set.range fun l : ULift.{u} ι => f l.down) = Set.range f from
237	        ULift.down_surjective.range_comp f]
238	      exact hspan)
239	    (fun l => ?_)
240	  rw [← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg
241	      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away (f l.down))) (fun _ => rfl) F,
242	    ← DivFamZar.mapAlgHom_eq_mapAlg
243	      (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away (f l.down))) (fun _ => rfl) G]
244	  exact h l.down
245	
246	/-! ## The `∃!` form -/
247	
248	/-- **The away-span glue, uniquely**: the glued class of `exists_glue_of_awaySpan` is the
249	unique class over `S` restricting to the given family, by `eq_of_awaySpan_eq`.  This is
250	the form the DDR-9 forward map consumes (`w4-ddr9` worksheet §3.4, "choice-independence
251	of the factorization"): a value characterized by an `∃!` does not depend on how the
252	cover was produced, so the forward map needs no separate well-definedness argument. -/
253	theorem existsUnique_glue_of_awaySpan {m : ℕ} (f : Fin m → S)
254	    (hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
255	    (F : ∀ p : Fin m, DivFamZar C (Localization.Away (f p)) π n)
256	    (hcompat : ∀ p q : Fin m,
257	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (awayMulLeft (k := k) f p q) (F p)
258	        = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (awayMulRight (k := k) f p q) (F q)) :
259	    ∃! F₀ : DivFamZar C S π n, ∀ p : Fin m,
260	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away (f p))) F₀ = F p := by
261	  obtain ⟨F₀, hF₀⟩ := exists_glue_of_awaySpan f hspan F hcompat
262	  exact ⟨F₀, hF₀, fun F₁ hF₁ =>
263	    eq_of_awaySpan_eq f hspan (fun p => (hF₁ p).trans (hF₀ p).symm)⟩
264	
265	end DivFamZar
266	
267	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# F5 — gluing the chart pulls of one morphism (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.4)
11	
12	The affine forward map of DDR-9 is built from three landed pieces:
13	
14	1. the atlas factorization `divScheme_exists_chartFactor`
15	   (`Picard/DivSchemeAtlasFactor.lean`) — a morphism `v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver`
16	   factors, over a finite spanning family `f : Fin m → S`, through carve charts along
17	   `k`-algebra maps `ω t : R_Z →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t)`;
18	2. the per-chart pull `divRepPullAt` (`Picard/DivRepAffKit.lean`) of a supplied
19	   universal chart family of `DivFamZar` classes;
20	3. the overlap agreement `divRepPullAt_mapAlgHom_eq_of_chartFactor`
21	   (`Picard/DivRepAffChartOverlap.lean`) — two chart presentations of the *same* `v`
22	   pull to the same class over any common tower ring.
23	
24	What was missing between them is the glue itself, and the reason is mechanical rather
25	than mathematical: (3) is stated over an abstract common ring `B` with an instance pack
26	in scope, while the gluing keystone needs the *canonical* overlap carrier
27	`Localization.Away (f p * f q)` together with its eight-field pack.
28	`Picard/DivRepAwaySpanGlue.lean` supplies that pack; this file uses it.
29	
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepPullAt_awayMul_compat` — **the overlap hypothesis in the
31	  canonical spelling**: the chart pulls of the pieces of one factorization agree along
32	  the two comparison maps into `Localization.Away (f p * f q)`.  This is (3) at the
33	  canonical carrier, with the comparison maps identified with the structure maps of the
34	  instance pack.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_divRepPullGlue` — **the glued pull**: the chart pulls glue
36	  to a class over `S` restricting to each piece.
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.existsUnique_divRepPullGlue` — the glued class is the *unique* one
38	  restricting to the pieces, so it is determined by the factorization data.
39	
40	Together these are the whole of the `pull` field's construction over a *given*
41	factorization.  Independence of the choice of factorization is a separate statement,
42	and it is the one that needs the DDR9-U ε-identity U2 — see the roadmap leaf
43	`AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2`.  Everything in this file is U2-free: it
44	consumes `DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible` as a hypothesis, exactly as
45	`Picard/DivRepAffChartOverlap.lean` does, and U2 is what will *prove* that hypothesis
46	for the universal family rather than what is needed to *use* it.
47	-/

103	/-! ## The overlap hypothesis at the canonical carrier -/
104	
105	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
106	-- The two `divRepPullAt` composites unfold `DivFamZar.mapAlgHom` through the chart-ring
107	-- notation while the instance pack of the canonical overlap carrier is being unified;
108	-- the defeq check is what costs (the I-0227 budget, as in the overlap lemma itself).
109	/-- **The overlap hypothesis of the chart pulls, in the canonical-carrier spelling.**
110	Two pieces `p`, `q` of one atlas factorization of `v` present the same morphism, so
111	their chart pulls agree after base change along the two comparison maps
112	`awayMulLeft`/`awayMulRight` into `Localization.Away (f p * f q)`.
113	
114	This is `divRepPullAt_mapAlgHom_eq_of_chartFactor` at the canonical overlap carrier: the
115	instance pack is built from the comparison maps themselves, so the abstract
116	`IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A B` of that lemma's conclusion *is* the comparison map, and
117	the two statements agree on the nose. -/
118	theorem divRepPullAt_awayMul_compat
119	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
120	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
121	    (hU : DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
122	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver)
123	    {m : ℕ} (f : Fin m → S)
124	    (ci : Fin m → (glueData k g r1).J) (cj : Fin m → (glueData k g r2).J)
125	    (cw : ∀ t : Fin m, ChartRing (ci t) (cj t) →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t))
126	    (hcw : ∀ t : Fin m,
127	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (cw t).toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap (ci t) (cj t)
128	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S (Localization.Away (f t)))) ≫ v.left)
129	    (p q : Fin m) :
130	    DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (DivFamZar.awayMulLeft (k := k) f p q)
131	        (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U (ci p) (cj p) (cw p))
132	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (DivFamZar.awayMulRight (k := k) f p q)
133	        (divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U (ci q) (cj q) (cw q)) := by
134	  classical
135	  -- the canonical overlap carrier receives both away carriers, by the comparison maps
136	  letI algL : Algebra (Localization.Away (f p)) (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) :=
137	    (DivFamZar.awayMulLeft (k := k) f p q).toRingHom.toAlgebra
138	  letI algR : Algebra (Localization.Away (f q)) (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) :=
139	    (DivFamZar.awayMulRight (k := k) f p q).toRingHom.toAlgebra
140	  haveI towSL : IsScalarTower S (Localization.Away (f p))
141	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) :=
142	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (RingHom.ext fun x => by
143	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
144	      exact (DivFamZar.awayMulOfDvd_algebraMap (k := k) (f p * f q) (f p) (f q)
145	        rfl x).symm)
146	  haveI towSR : IsScalarTower S (Localization.Away (f q))
147	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) :=
148	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (RingHom.ext fun x => by
149	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
150	      exact (DivFamZar.awayMulOfDvd_algebraMap (k := k) (f p * f q) (f q) (f p)
151	        (mul_comm _ _) x).symm)
152	  haveI towkL : IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away (f p))
153	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) :=
154	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (RingHom.ext fun x => by
155	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
156	      exact ((DivFamZar.awayMulLeft (k := k) f p q).commutes x).symm)
157	  haveI towkR : IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away (f q))
158	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) :=
159	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (RingHom.ext fun x => by
160	      rw [RingHom.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
161	      exact ((DivFamZar.awayMulRight (k := k) f p q).commutes x).symm)
162	  -- the abstract tower maps of the overlap lemma ARE the two comparison maps
163	  have hL : IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k (Localization.Away (f p))
164	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) = DivFamZar.awayMulLeft (k := k) f p q :=
165	    AlgHom.ext fun x => by
166	      change algebraMap (Localization.Away (f p)) (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) x = _
167	      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
168	      rfl
169	  have hR : IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k (Localization.Away (f q))
170	      (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) = DivFamZar.awayMulRight (k := k) f p q :=
171	    AlgHom.ext fun x => by
172	      change algebraMap (Localization.Away (f q)) (Localization.Away (f p * f q)) x = _
173	      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
174	      rfl
175	  rw [← hL, ← hR]
176	  exact divRepPullAt_mapAlgHom_eq_of_chartFactor hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 U hU v
177	    (cw p) (cw q) (hcw p) (hcw q)
178	
179	/-! ## The glued pull over a given factorization -/
180	
181	/-- **The glued pull of a factorization**: the chart pulls of the pieces of an atlas
182	factorization of `v` glue to a locally certified class over `S` restricting to each
183	piece.  Existence is `DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_awaySpan` fed by
184	`divRepPullAt_awayMul_compat`. -/
185	theorem exists_divRepPullGlue
186	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
187	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
188	    (hU : DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
189	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver)
190	    {m : ℕ} (f : Fin m → S) (hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
191	    (ci : Fin m → (glueData k g r1).J) (cj : Fin m → (glueData k g r2).J)
192	    (cw : ∀ t : Fin m, ChartRing (ci t) (cj t) →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t))
193	    (hcw : ∀ t : Fin m,
194	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (cw t).toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap (ci t) (cj t)
195	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S (Localization.Away (f t)))) ≫ v.left) :
196	    ∃ F₀ : DivFamZar C S pi g, ∀ t : Fin m,
197	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away (f t))) F₀
198	        = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U (ci t) (cj t) (cw t) :=
199	  DivFamZar.exists_glue_of_awaySpan f hspan
200	    (fun t => divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U (ci t) (cj t) (cw t))
201	    (divRepPullAt_awayMul_compat hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 U hU v f ci cj cw hcw)
202	
203	/-- **The glued pull is unique**: no two classes over `S` restrict to the same family of
204	chart pulls, by Zariski separation over the factorization's spanning family.  So the
205	`pull` field's value is determined by the factorization data, with no further choice —
206	what remains for full choice-independence is comparing two *different* factorizations,
207	which is the U2-gated statement. -/
208	theorem existsUnique_divRepPullGlue
209	    (U : ∀ (i : (glueData k g r1).J) (j : (glueData k g r2).J),
210	      DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g)
211	    (hU : DivRepChartFamily.IsCompatible (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U)
212	    {S : Type u} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver)
213	    {m : ℕ} (f : Fin m → S) (hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤)
214	    (ci : Fin m → (glueData k g r1).J) (cj : Fin m → (glueData k g r2).J)
215	    (cw : ∀ t : Fin m, ChartRing (ci t) (cj t) →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t))
216	    (hcw : ∀ t : Fin m,
217	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (cw t).toRingHom) ≫ ChartMap (ci t) (cj t)
218	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S (Localization.Away (f t)))) ≫ v.left) :
219	    ∃! F₀ : DivFamZar C S pi g, ∀ t : Fin m,
220	      DivFamZar.mapAlgHom (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k S (Localization.Away (f t))) F₀
221	        = divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U (ci t) (cj t) (cw t) :=
222	  DivFamZar.existsUnique_glue_of_awaySpan f hspan
223	    (fun t => divRepPullAt (hpi := hpi) g r1 r2 b1 b2 U (ci t) (cj t) (cw t))
224	    (divRepPullAt_awayMul_compat hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 U hU v f ci cj cw hcw)
225	
226	end Curve

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffPullGlue
7	
8	/-!
9	# F5 — the glued pull does not depend on the factorization, and it is U2-free
10	
11	`Picard/DivRepAffPullGlue.lean` glues the chart pulls of ONE atlas factorization of a
12	morphism `v : overSpec k S ⟶ DivOver` into a class over `S`, uniquely determined by that
13	factorization's data.  What was still owed for the `pull` field of
14	`DivRepAffinePullback` is that two *different* factorizations of the same `v` give the
15	same class.
16	
17	`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.4 lists this as "choice-independence of the
18	factorization", and the roadmap leaf `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2` describes
19	the affine package as "U2 + choice bookkeeping", which reads as though this bookkeeping
20	were downstream of the DDR9-U ε-identity.  **It is not.**  The reason is a property of
21	the landed overlap lemma that nobody had used:
22	
23	> `divRepPullAt_mapAlgHom_eq_of_chartFactor` (`Picard/DivRepAffChartOverlap.lean`)
24	> compares **any two chart presentations of the same morphism `v`**, over any two
25	> carriers `A`, `A'`, restricted to any common tower ring `B`.  It never asks that the
26	> two presentations come from the same factorization.
27	
28	So the cross-refinement of two factorizations is handled by exactly the lemma that
29	handles one factorization's own overlaps.  Concretely: the products `f p * f' q` of two
30	spanning families span the unit ideal (`span_mul_span_of_span_eq_top`), the canonical
31	carrier `Localization.Away (f p * f' q)` receives both `Localization.Away (f p)` and
32	`Localization.Away (f' q)` by the comparison maps of
33	`Picard/DivRepAwaySpanGlue.lean`, and the two glued classes agree there.
34	
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.span_mul_span_of_span_eq_top` — products of two spanning families
36	  span the unit ideal.
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divRepPullGlue_eq_of_chartFactors` — **factorization-independence**:
38	  two classes over `S`, each restricting to the chart pulls of its own factorization of
39	  the same `v`, are equal.
40	
41	With this, the `pull` field of `DivRepAffinePullback` is a well-defined function of `v`
42	alone, over a supplied compatible chart family, with no residual choice and no ε-identity
43	consumed.  What genuinely remains U2-gated is the *other* two fields —
44	`isDivRepClassify_pull` (the pulled class satisfies the characterizing clause, which is
45	where the ε-identity enters) — together with `IsCompatible` for the universal family
46	itself.
47	-/
48	
49	set_option autoImplicit false
50	set_option quotPrecheck false
51	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
52	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
53	
54	universe u
55	
56	open CategoryTheory
57	
58	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
59	
60	open Grassmannian Scheme
61	
62	/-! ## Products of two spanning families span -/
63	
64	/-- **Products of two spanning families span the unit ideal**: the ideal generated by the
65	products `f p * f' q` contains the product of the two unit ideals, hence is the unit
66	ideal.  This is the cross-refinement of two covers of `Spec R`. -/
67	theorem span_mul_span_of_span_eq_top {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {m m' : ℕ}
68	    (f : Fin m → R) (f' : Fin m' → R)
69	    (h : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤) (h' : Ideal.span (Set.range f') = ⊤) :
70	    Ideal.span (Set.range fun pq : Fin m × Fin m' => f pq.1 * f' pq.2) = ⊤ := by
71	  have key : Ideal.span (Set.range f) * Ideal.span (Set.range f')
72	      ≤ Ideal.span (Set.range fun pq : Fin m × Fin m' => f pq.1 * f' pq.2) := by
73	    rw [Ideal.span_mul_span]
74	    refine Ideal.span_le.mpr ?_
75	    rintro x ⟨a, ⟨p, rfl⟩, b, ⟨q, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
76	    exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨(p, q), rfl⟩
77	  rw [h, h'] at key
78	  simpa using key
79	
80	section Curve

--- theorem ---
variable (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))

/-- **The chart atlas of `DivScheme g`** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.3): each
`Z(♦)`-chart `Spec R_Z` maps to `DivScheme g`, factoring the chart presentation through
`divSchemeι`.  The kill law is `divCarveIdeal_le_ker_of_tower` at the chart ring itself
(spelled `Ideal.mk_ker`). -/
noncomputable def divCarveChartToDivScheme
    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
    Spec (CommRingCat.of (DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j))
      ⟶ DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ :=
  carveLocusToCarveScheme k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j

/-- **The defining triangle of the `DivScheme` chart atlas**: through the closed immersion
`divSchemeι`, the chart map of `Spec R_Z` is `Spec` of the quotient presentation
`divCarveChartMk` followed by the pair chart. -/
theorem divCarveChartToDivScheme_divSchemeι
    (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J) :
    divCarveChartToDivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j ≫ divSchemeι k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (divCarveChartMk k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j).toRingHom)
        ≫ pairChartMap k g r₁ g r₂ i j :=
  carveLocusToCarveScheme_carveSchemeι k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) i j

/-- **The atlas factorization of `DivScheme g`** (`informal/w4-ddr9-worksheet.md` §3.3,
the DDR-9.F1 keystone): every test morphism `v : overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver` factors,
over a finite spanning family of basic localizations of `S`, through some chart
`divCarveChartToDivScheme i j` along a `k`-algebra map
`ω : R_Z →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t)` out of the `Z(♦)`-chart ring. -/
theorem divScheme_exists_chartFactor (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    (v : overSpec k S ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : Fin m → S), Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ t : Fin m, ∃ (i : (glueData k g r₁).J) (j : (glueData k g r₂).J)
        (ω : DivCarveChartRing k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (f t)),
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ω.toRingHom)
            ≫ divCarveChartToDivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ i j
          = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S (Localization.Away (f t))))
            ≫ v.left :=
  carveScheme_exists_chartFactor k g r₁ r₂ (divCarveMul k A B r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) S v

8	/-!
9	# Pushing an away cover forward along an algebra map
10	
11	The `pull_naturality` field of `DivRepAffinePullback` compares the forward map at `A` with
12	the forward map at `B` along a `k`-algebra map `φ : A →ₐ[k] B`.  The forward map is built
13	from an atlas factorization over a spanning family `f : Fin m → A`, so naturality needs the
14	*pushed* family `φ ∘ f : Fin m → B` and the induced comparison of carriers.
15	
16	This file supplies that transport, at the canonical carriers, over `k`:
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.awayPush` — the induced `k`-algebra map
19	  `Localization.Away a →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (φ a)`, i.e. mathlib's
20	  `Localization.awayMap` upgraded over the base field.  Characterized by
21	  `awayPush_algebraMap`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.awayPush_comp_toAlgHom` — the square with the two structure
23	  maps: pushing forward after restricting to `Localization.Away a` is restricting to
24	  `Localization.Away (φ a)` after `φ`.  This is the identity that turns naturality of the
25	  forward map into a statement about the pushed cover.
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.span_range_map_eq_top` — the pushed family still spans, so
27	  it is again an admissible cover.
28	
29	Nothing here mentions divisors: it is the localization bookkeeping the naturality field
30	needs, isolated so that the naturality proof itself reads as a comparison of glued values.
31	-/
32

34	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
35	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

40	
41	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
42	
43	namespace DivFamZar

45	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
46	variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
47	
48	/-! ## The pushed carrier -/
49	
50	/-- **The comparison of away carriers along an algebra map**: mathlib's
51	`Localization.awayMap` of `φ` at `a`, upgraded to a map of `k`-algebras.  Both structure
52	maps factor through `φ`, which is what makes it one. -/
53	noncomputable def awayPush (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) (a : A) :
54	    Localization.Away a →ₐ[k] Localization.Away (φ a) :=
55	  { Localization.awayMap φ.toRingHom a with
56	    commutes' := fun x => by
57	      rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k A (Localization.Away a)]
58	      change Localization.awayMap φ.toRingHom a
59	        (algebraMap A (Localization.Away a) (algebraMap k A x)) = _
60	      rw [show Localization.awayMap φ.toRingHom a
61	              (algebraMap A (Localization.Away a) (algebraMap k A x))
62	            = algebraMap B (Localization.Away (φ a)) (φ (algebraMap k A x)) by
63	          simp [Localization.awayMap, IsLocalization.Away.map], φ.commutes]
64	      exact (IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply k B (Localization.Away (φ a)) x).symm }
65	
66	/-- **The characterizing property of `awayPush`**: on the image of `A` it is `φ` followed by
67	the structure map of the pushed carrier. -/
68	@[simp]
69	theorem awayPush_algebraMap (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) (a : A) (x : A) :
70	    awayPush φ a (algebraMap A (Localization.Away a) x)
71	      = algebraMap B (Localization.Away (φ a)) (φ x) := by
72	  simp [awayPush, Localization.awayMap, IsLocalization.Away.map]
73	
74	set_option maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
75	-- The composite is checked against the `IsScalarTower` structure maps of two localizations
76	-- at once, which unfolds the section-ring algebra towers on both sides; the defeq check is
77	-- well past the default budget (as for `awayMulOfDvd_toAlgHom`).
78	/-- **The naturality square of the away carriers**: restricting to `Localization.Away a` and
79	then pushing forward along `φ` is the same as applying `φ` and then restricting to
80	`Localization.Away (φ a)`.  This is the identity that converts `pull_naturality` into a
81	comparison over the pushed cover. -/
82	theorem awayPush_comp_toAlgHom (φ : A →ₐ[k] B) (a : A) :
83	    (awayPush φ a).comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A (Localization.Away a))
84	      = (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k B (Localization.Away (φ a))).comp φ :=
85	  AlgHom.ext fun x => awayPush_algebraMap φ a x
86	
87	/-! ## The pushed cover is a cover -/

# Concurrent-lane protocol (2026-07-16, from inbox I-0149's incidents — BINDING for parallel agent fleets)

Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
workspace.

## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)

All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:

```bash
cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>

Archon-Commit: agent
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
```

If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.

### 1b. The CAS recipe leaves the SHARED index permanently stale — this is by design, and it is armed

Added 2026-07-27 (run 0048 r5) after this failed a **third** time (`I-0366`: the shared index
was pinned to a pre-round-5 snapshot and a bare `git commit` would have deleted
`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean` and un-rooted it from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in one commit).

The mechanism is not a bug in anyone's lane, it is the direct consequence of §1: a CAS commit
publishes a tree built in a **private** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and moves the ref with `update-ref`.
The **shared** index is never touched, so the moment anybody commits, the shared index still
describes the previous HEAD — and `git status` then reports that difference as *staged changes*,
including **staged deletions** for any file the commit added. The longer a run goes, the further
the shared index drifts behind.

Consequences, all three binding:

1. **Never run a bare `git commit` (no `-a`, no pathspec) against `workspace.git`.** It publishes
   whatever the stale shared index holds, which is a reversion of other lanes' work.
2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).

Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.

## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there

`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:

```bash
LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
